brief: UBS's Daily US covers Monday's rebound from last week's AI-driven selloff. The S&P 500 rose 4.7%, Nasdaq 100 6.9%, and NVIDIA 31.5%, helped by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. Treasury yields edged up, gold rebounded 3% after a 9% weekly drop, and Asian indices jumped Tuesday. Last week the Nasdaq fell around 10% (steepest since March 2020, down 19.8% from its October 6 high and near bear market territory) and the S&P fell 8.6% into correction territory. UBS does not see the AI investment story as broken but expects more differentiation between well-funded platforms and those dependent on debt or scarce capacity, and keeps global and US equities Neutral given elevated expectations. It uses the bounce to recommend trimming overlapping megacap tech for Eurozone equities, industrials, healthcare, and equal-weight strategies. Within AI it favors quality compute and foundry names over leveraged capacity providers, recommends rebalancing into intermediate-duration bonds and 7-8%-yielding high-yield and emerging-market debt, and favors adding gold, kept Attractive and targeting USD 5,000/oz by December 2027, and hedge funds. Separately, UBS prefers China's onshore A-shares, kept Attractive, over H-shares, kept Neutral, on an AI self-sufficiency theme, as offshore names like Alibaba and Tencent post cloud growth but lagging monetization.
